A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 20-page versions of the same CoSo study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoSo experiments on mobile control, card games, and embodied tasks, including ablations, an LLM-agent extension, and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–2, Appendices C–D, and the exploration and ablation figures.

M1.justification: The counterfactual token weighting, causal-weighted entropy objective, Algorithm 1, and AWR/PPO integrations are unchanged. Adding the BERT citation in Section 4.4 does not introduce a different model or procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AitW General and WebShopping, four Gym Cards tasks, six ALFWorld task types, and the text-only AlfredTWEnv extension. Appendix C's LLM-agent evaluation already appears in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, C.1, D.1, and the ablations. Digi-Q and DistRL are newly cited in v2 but are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported splits, task limits, models, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. This includes Appendix C's Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct training without SFT for 12,000 environment steps.

E4.justification: Both retain the WebShopping/NumberLine entropy ablation, token-importance analyses, action-sampling case studies, and computational-overhead comparison. Sections 5.2–5.3 and Appendices D–F introduce no additional analysis.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same three-random-seed reporting, Table 1 retains its uncertainty values, and Figure 4 retains shaded bands. No new run counts, uncertainty procedures, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2, C.1, and D.1 retain all result entries and values. CoSo's reported averages remain 72.9% for AitW, 49.3% for Gym Cards, 26.5% for ALFWorld, and 39.6% for AlfredTWEnv. The plotted trends and qualitative examples also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The SCM assumption, policy-evaluation/improvement statements, and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical substance. Equation (6) changes equivalent scalar norm notation, while Appendix A.1 adds an explanatory conditional-entropy gloss; neither revises the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about targeted exploration, convergence, policy improvement, and applicability across agent tasks. The claimed relative performance gains of 12.3%, 9.3%, and 16.7% are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting action-critical tokens to efficient exploration are retained. Section 6 still limits the evidence to utterances shorter than 300 tokens and identifies ultra-long chain-of-thought effectiveness as unexplored.

D1.justification: The code-access information, implementation descriptions, and Appendix B hyperparameters are unchanged, including the 0.01B-parameter SCM, learning rate of 1e-5, and entropy coefficient of 1.0. Appendix D retains the same H100 resource information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Digi-Q and DistRL to Section 2 and cites Devlin et al. for BERT in Section 4.4. These are limited attribution additions without substantial repositioning. The Brohan-to-Zitkovich RT-2 citation change identifies the same work, as do the other publication-metadata updates.

P1.justification: v2 adds funding acknowledgements, removes the Skywork AI affiliation, corrects the conference ordinal, updates bibliography formatting, and adds the entropy gloss. The narrative structure is retained. Section 3 also introduces an inconsistent '|V| = 30k' annotation beside the unchanged 32,100-token example.

P2.justification: The author block is compacted and the acknowledgements and references cause limited reflow. Figures 4 and E.2 have small rendering differences while retaining their plotted content, axes, and captions. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain essentially identical, including the appendices. Additional citations and funding disclosure provide modest editorial benefits, while the new vocabulary-size annotation introduces a small inconsistency. These limited changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
